headline: High: ECC’s writable, networked, MCP-enabled defaults can cascade Dagster-derived outputs into unsafe actions; prompt-injection and compliance risks are lower but nonzero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dagster has no direct I/O surfaces, but ECC ingests files, stdin/stdout, and MCP by default, so any Dagster-produced content that reaches ECC can be treated as instruction-like input. The pair lacks a documented shared channel, so this is inferred rather than observed, but the interaction is plausible and not blocked by either profile.
conditions: IF Dagster outputs are copied into ECC prompts, files, or MCP payloads
IF ECC parses imported content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable copy-paste of Dagster outputs into ECC sessions
Add a provenance prefix to all Dagster-generated text
Restrict ECC MCP tools to read-only during review
Use a separate workspace for Dagster artifacts
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dagster is local-only with no filesystem read/write or network egress, while ECC can read/write files and call external APIs. The pair does not show a shared workspace by default, so leakage requires an unusual local setup, but if they share files, ECC can exfiltrate content it reads.
conditions: IF Dagster artifacts are placed in a directory ECC can read
IF ECC is configured to send those artifacts to its allowed external APIs
mitigations: Keep Dagster and ECC in separate directories
Do not place secrets in shared project files
Review ECC API integrations before enabling them
Use OS permissions to block ECC from Dagster workspaces
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the orchestrator level

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dagster itself has no write or network capabilities, but ECC has unrestricted filesystem write, git modification, subprocesses, and allowlisted egress. If both operate on the same repo or config tree, ECC can overwrite files Dagster depends on; uncertainty is limited because ECC explicitly supports shared-state scenarios.
conditions: IF both agents target the same repository or config directory
IF ECC writes files that Dagster later reads or deploys
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Pause ECC writes during Dagster runs
Use git branches per agent
Check in a lockfile or lease file before edits
requires-engineering: add cross-agent locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: ECC is designed around skills, hooks, and agent definitions, so it can readily act on upstream text. Dagster can emit pipeline metadata or findings, and if ECC treats those outputs as authoritative, it may commit, publish, or configure downstream actions without verification. The pairwise pathway is inferred from documented surfaces, not directly sandboxed.
conditions: IF Dagster outputs are fed into ECC skills, hooks, or agent definitions
IF ECC executes or publishes actions without an explicit verification step
mitigations: Require human review before ECC acts on Dagster outputs
Mark Dagster outputs as untrusted in ECC workflows
Disable auto-apply hooks for shared pipelines
Add a verification checklist before commits or API calls
requires-engineering: implement signed, schema-validated handoff records

E_compliance.rationale: Dagster touches no sensitive classes in the profile, but ECC explicitly handles session summaries, agent definitions, git history, security findings, and multiple config files with retention-related secrets. Because ECC’s retention and data-home settings are exposed while Dagster’s are not, the pair presents a policy-mismatch risk if shared data is routed into ECC; the other agent is not cited for residency because none is declared.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in ECC session summaries or git history
IF ECC retention settings differ from the organization’s required retention
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in ECC-managed files
Set ECC retention to the minimum allowed value
Review which data classes are written to git history
Document a deletion/export process for ECC artifacts
requires-engineering: align ECC storage and retention with policy
